reasons: One-time code digits are not enforced.
The provider rule for Google and Apple is unverified.
Duplicate class names exist in another file.
No tests for these rules are visible in this packet.

terms.meaning: a data shape: a class that lists which fields a request must carry
checks run on incoming data before it is used
a label written above a field that tells the framework which rule to apply
a tool that builds human-readable API documentation from these labels

used_by: Auth controller files, not in this packet

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for validation and API docs
sections.what: Brings in the validation rules, such as must be an email, and the labels that describe fields in the API docs.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app check input before it reaches the auth logic and produce API documentation.

sections.name: SendOtpDto
sections.title: Request to send a one-time code
sections.what: Defines the input for sending a code: an optional phone and an optional email, each checked for correct format.
sections.why: Likely reason: sending a code needs one contact detail, so each field is optional.
sections.watch_out: Neither field is required, so an empty request passes validation and only fails later in the service.

sections.name: VerifyOtpDto
sections.title: Request to check a one-time code
sections.what: Defines the input for checking a code: an optional phone or email, plus a six-character code.
sections.why: Likely reason: the code must be matched to the same contact it was sent to.
sections.watch_out: The code is checked only for length, not for digits, so any six characters pass.

sections.name: RegisterDto
sections.title: Sign-up form rules
sections.what: Defines the input for email and password sign-up: a valid email, a strong password with at least eight characters, a full name of 2 to 100 characters, an optional phone, and an optional list of consent purposes.
sections.why: Likely reason: sign-up is the point where strong password rules must be enforced.
sections.watch_out: The consent list is not checked against allowed values, so any text can be stored as a consent purpose.

sections.name: LoginDto
sections.title: Login form rules
sections.what: Defines the input for password sign-in: email, password and optional device details. The password only needs one character here.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Login does not enforce password strength, so the strong password rule applies only at sign-up and reset.

sections.name: OAuthLoginDto
sections.title: Sign-in with Google or Apple
sections.what: Defines the input for Google or Apple sign-in: the provider name, the ID token from that provider, and optional name and device details.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app receives the provider's token and checks it on the server.
sections.watch_out: The provider rule may not reject unknown providers, which is unverified in this file.

sections.name: RefreshTokenDto
sections.title: Request to renew a session token
sections.what: Defines the input carrying the refresh token used to get a new access token.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: A copy of this class also exists in the send-otp file, so a change to one may not reach the other.

sections.name: ForgotPasswordDto
sections.title: Request for a password reset
sections.what: Defines the input for forgotten password: an email address that must be valid.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Reset emails are not sent yet, so this request does not reach the user.

sections.name: ResetPasswordDto
sections.title: Setting a new password with a reset token
sections.what: Defines the input for resetting a password: the token from the reset email and a new strong password.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Password strength rules are copied across several classes, so they can drift apart if one is changed.

sections.name: ChangePasswordDto
sections.title: Changing password while signed in
sections.what: Defines the input for changing a password: the current password and a new strong password.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Nothing here or in the service stops the new password from matching the old one.

sections.name: RegisterBiometricDto
sections.title: Registering a device biometric key
sections.what: Defines the input for storing a device biometric public key and an optional device name.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The key is checked only to be non-empty text, not for its format.

sections.name: BiometricLoginDto
sections.title: Signing in with a device biometric
sections.what: Defines the input for biometric sign-in: a signed challenge and the session ID from registration.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The signature is required here, yet the login service never checks it.

sections.name: RevokeSessionDto
sections.title: Naming a session to sign out
sections.what: Defines the input carrying the ID of the session to end.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

summary: Defines the shapes and validation rules for the request data that auth endpoints accept.
purpose: Checks what each auth request must contain before the service code runs, and feeds the API documentation.
why: Likely reason: rejects bad input early, at the edge of the app. Reason beyond that not stated in the code.
how: Each class lists fields. Decorators on each field check format, length or strength. Documentation labels describe each field for the API docs.
inputs: Raw request bodies sent to the auth endpoints.
outputs: Either a checked object for the service, or a rejection with an error message naming the failing field.
risks: Consent purposes are not checked against allowed values. One-time code digits are not enforced. The Google and Apple provider rule may not reject unknown providers (unverified). Password strength rules are copied across several classes. Two classes share names with classes in the send-otp file.
debug: If a request is rejected, read the error message, which names the failing field, then check the rule on that field. The app setup (not in this packet) must enable validation for these rules to run.
